llm.summary: The skill is not clearly malicious, but it needs review because it is a cloud audio-transcription tool whose trigger text incorrectly points to translation/localization and whose privacy implications are under-emphasized.

dimensions.detail: The skill requires Azure credentials and audio made available through Blob URLs, and it processes potentially sensitive recordings through Azure cloud services; this is expected for the purpose but should be scoped and disclosed more clearly.
dimensions.label: Credentials
dimensions.name: environment_proportionality

dimensions.detail: The artifact is Markdown only but requests exec and instructs installing the azure-ai-transcription Python package; that is purpose-aligned for an SDK-based transcription workflow, and no bundled executable scripts were present.
dimensions.label: Install Mechanism
dimensions.name: install_mechanism

dimensions.detail: The trigger condition says to use the skill for text translation, multilingual conversion, and localization, which is mismatched with the actual audio transcription capability and could route unrelated or sensitive text tasks to the wrong workflow.
dimensions.label: Instruction Scope
dimensions.name: instruction_scope

dimensions.detail: No background workers, persistence, privilege escalation, credential harvesting, or hidden long-running behavior were found; credentials are described as environment variables and outputs are transcript/SRT files.
dimensions.label: Persistence & Privilege
dimensions.name: persistence_privilege

dimensions.detail: The main capability, using Azure AI Speech Transcription for audio-to-text and timestamped transcripts, is coherent with the stated purpose; the generic create/query/modify/delete wording is vague but no destructive artifact behavior was found.
dimensions.label: Purpose & Capability
dimensions.name: purpose_capability

llm.guidance: Install only if you specifically want Azure-based speech-to-text. Do not rely on this skill for translation or localization tasks. Before using it with meetings, interviews, or other sensitive recordings, confirm you are allowed to upload the audio to Blob storage and process it with Azure, and protect the TRANSCRIPTION_KEY as a credential.
llm.findings:
[SQP-1] unexpected: Accepted as a material review concern: the artifact's trigger text names translation/localization rather than audio transcription, creating a real purpose mismatch.
[SQP-2] expected: Cloud processing is inherent to this Azure transcription purpose and is partially disclosed through Azure and Blob references, but the artifact lacks a clear privacy notice for audio URLs, uploaded audio, and transcript content leaving the local environment.
